summary.intent: Finish and publish the last Caliper trail branches (agent-eval weekly, three-tools report) as PRs, then understand what the accuracy and performance numbers mean, which opt-ins the weekly measurement uses, and whether those should become defaults.
summary.outcome: Opened PRs #313 (agent-eval) and #314 (three-tools oracle report), and summarized accuracy (recall vs RDT, checker oracle) and performance (time/memory vs RDT and react-docgen) from the latest weekly record. The check of which flags the weekly run uses and the option defaults was started but its result was not yet reported.

repo: The weekly CI job builds only the CLI, not the NAPI slice, so the agent-eval reads the whole-output TOON table plus JSON diagnostics.
`just lint` caps files at 300 lines; oracle.ts was kept at 292 by moving logic into tool-score.ts and tool-universe.ts.
The weekly record keeps `oracle.shared_props`, `agree` and `wrong` stable; new per-tool data goes under `oracle.tools`.

Caliper's whole-universe agreement (~40%) is mostly a definition effect: the checker-defined universe includes non-component exported functions and collapsed inheritance layers are counted separately.
RDT prints unnameable types as `{string}`; treating this as unreadable cut its wrong rate on shadcn from 8.9% to 0.6%.
Default now loads dependency types, costing roughly 70 ms and 175 MiB on shadcn and ~4.8x wall time on Chakra versus without them.
The justfile's stricter test invocation flags tool-norm.test.ts, as it already did on main.

code.finding: The comment claiming it 'reads each file alone' was inaccurate and was corrected in the three-tools branch.
RDT's `{string}` is now read as unreadable, scoring as less precise rather than wrong.

workflow: After pushing a branch, the PR link can fail because the remote hasn't registered it yet; waiting a few seconds and retrying works.
Stating that CI checks were not read, and which paths were not validated end to end, keeps PR reports honest.
Pull the real weekly record before answering questions about numbers rather than answering from memory.

friction: PR link step failed on first attempt because the remote had not registered the pushed branch yet.
The new oracle numbers (whole-universe vs of-listed shares) confused the user, who asked what the numbers mean.
Caliper's oracle numbers were produced from an Oct-30 binary, not a fresh build.
CI weekly timings are noisy on a shared machine; RDT and react-docgen were measured with only one run each.
